guarantee.name: Guarantee of Temporary Residence and Labour
guarantee.line: No. VS-18-0947. Thirty days, and you signed on the line for the person guaranteed. If it lapses unrenewed, you leave within seven days.

ticket.name: Railway ticket
ticket.line: You had it gripped in your hand when you came out of the chambers.

hunt.name: The hunt invitation from Millridge
hunt.line: The wax carries the Duke’s arms; the hand inside is Baron Henk’s. A small line at the foot: Her Grace the Duke will be present at the opening this year.

letter.name: The chancery’s letter
letter.line: Beneath the progress summary, an addendum: the guarantee expires on the thirtieth of October, and a renewal must be submitted not later than seven days before.

broker.name: The broker’s note
broker.line: No name on it. Only: “Willing to trade in kind, prices as the market goes, will call at the house.”

ledger.name: The sheet you copied
ledger.line: Hartmann’s last two months of sundry expenditure, copied by date. Three to five guldmark each, in a careful hand, nothing crossed out.

brush.name: The second brush
brush.line: A shorter handle, used longer. “This one sits better,” Gregor said. The next day it hung on a hook by the stable door, on its own.

fruit.name: A small bag of dried fruit
fruit.line: A tenant’s wife made it. He put the bag in your hands and went, as though afraid you would hand it back. You had not seen the fruit before. Very sweet.

pencil.name: A freshly sharpened pencil
pencil.line: On the corner of the desk, where there had been none. That day Elena stood a while without going, and said thank you.

sprig.name: The sprig in the folio
sprig.line: Pressed flat, the colour gone to pale brown.

variants.asked: Pressed flat, the colour gone to pale brown. You took it to Elena; she said she had not touched what was inside.
variants.replaced: Pressed flat, the colour gone to pale brown. You put it back between the same two leaves.

bark.name: The drawing on birch bark
bark.line: The stumps, the spacing, the line of the skid road, in charcoal. In the blank part Thierry added two strokes: a line for the stream, a cross for where it ran before it moved. Pressed inside an old folio in the office.

bottle.name: Thierry’s bottle
bottle.line: He handed it over at the street corner, half full and still warm. “Keep the bottle.”

coin.name: The guldmark from Henk
coin.line: “Get something for the horse on the road.” He did not sit down again.

purse.name: The cloth bag from Millridge
purse.line: He counted it through in front of you and pushed it across. “Call it a loan from me. Repay it whenever.” You put it in an inside pocket; it was heavier than you expected.

tin.name: The last steward’s tin
tin.line: Under a loose board in the office. A few coins, and half a sheet in a careful hand. Mostly figures; one line is not: an empty account, and a valley that has stopped speaking well of you, is a thing no letter of guarantee will hold against.
